how: GET localhost:3360/v1/principles/principles (athena-make, prod) and GET /principles/principles on the card's principles-api build against the same pod, same minute

athenaMake.name: hemenway-biological-renewable-resources
athenaMake.label: Use biological and renewable resources
athenaMake.comment: Renewable resources — usually living beings and their products — reproduce and build up over time, store energy, assist yield, and interact with other elements. Favor these over nonrenewable resources.
athenaMake.jeffReading: 'Focus is infrastructure' is this in practice — Jeff's finite attention is the resource every protocol and automation exists to conserve.
athenaMake.source: Hemenway, T. Gaia's Garden, 2nd ed., p. 7.
athenaMake.techReading: Patterns, skills, hooks, memory — recurring value — over one-shot human effort. Invest in the pattern, not the individual fix. Treat Jeff's attention as the renewable-but-finite resource the whole system is designed to protect.

athenaMake.name: hemenway-catch-and-store
athenaMake.label: Catch and store energy and materials
athenaMake.comment: Identify, collect, and hold useful flows. Every cycle is an opportunity for yield; every gradient (in slope, charge, temperature, or otherwise) is an opportunity for energy.
athenaMake.jeffReading: When Jeff has a live insight (a thought, write, reading), he cards it or stories it. The 2-month rule: capture-while-warm, not-on-discipline. Retires things — principles, cards, protocols, names — when they stop producing.
athenaMake.source: Hemenway, T. Gaia's Garden, 2nd ed., p. 6.
athenaMake.techReading: Capture events, insights, and decisions while warm — Chorus index, spine events, memory records, stories. TTL. Produce-no-waste corollary: every output of one element is input to another. Retire what does not earn its place.

athenaMake.name: hemenway-collaborate-with-succession
athenaMake.label: Collaborate with succession
athenaMake.comment: Living systems usually advance from immaturity to maturity, and if we accept this trend and align our designs with it instead of fighting it, we save work and energy. Mature ecosystems are more diverse and productive than young ones.
athenaMake.jeffReading: Jeff rebrands things (Bridge → Clearing, multiple Werk generations, Chorus rewrites) without sentimental attachment. The name is less important than the fit.
athenaMake.source: Hemenway, T. Gaia's Garden, 2nd ed., p. 7.
athenaMake.techReading: Refactor, retire, rename. Protocol versions grow up. The 10-week zero-to-self-healing Chorus delta is this principle in action. Cards move through Next → WIP → Done; principles move from practice to rule to invariant.

athenaMake.name: hemenway-connect
athenaMake.label: Connect
athenaMake.comment: Use relative location — place the elements of your design in ways that create useful relationships and time-saving connections among all parts. The number of connections among useful elements makes a healthy, diverse ecosystem, not the number of elements.
athenaMake.jeffReading: Jeff uses the team as a thinking partner, not as executors. Asks all three roles and composes the answers rather than directing one.
athenaMake.source: Hemenway, T. Gaia's Garden, 2nd ed., p. 6.
athenaMake.techReading: Roles compose, not isolate. Gates stay in-role (not in subagents). The Clearing. Pair work. Briefs move between roles directly.

athenaMake.name: hemenway-creativity-is-the-limit
athenaMake.label: The biggest limit to abundance is creativity
athenaMake.comment: The designer's imagination and skill usually limit productivity and diversity before any physical limits are reached.
athenaMake.jeffReading: Jeff's friction with 'agent-shaped answers' — rejects solutions that pattern-match without imagining what a human would actually want.
athenaMake.source: Hemenway, T. Gaia's Garden, 2nd ed., p. 7.
athenaMake.techReading: The hard constraint is rarely compute, lines of code, or token budget — it's the sharpness of the design question. Agent-shaped solutions fail the creativity test before they fail the engineering test.

athenaMake.name: hemenway-each-element-multiple-functions
athenaMake.label: Each element performs multiple functions
athenaMake.comment: Choose and place each element in a design so that it performs as many functions as possible. Beneficial connections between diverse components create a stable whole. Stack elements in both space and time.
athenaMake.jeffReading: Jeff reuses patterns he invented (briefs, demos, gates) across new problems rather than inventing new abstractions per problem. Compresses rather than proliferates.
athenaMake.source: Hemenway, T. Gaia's Garden, 2nd ed., p. 6.
athenaMake.techReading: Each role carries several functions (Wren = PM + moderator + interaction-layer owner; Kade = engineer + gate-code + gate-quality; Silas = architect + ops + repo-infra). Each primitive serves multiple skills (chorus-log, git-queue.sh, nudge). Stack in time: briefs become stories become principles.

athenaMake.name: hemenway-function-supported-by-multiple-elements
athenaMake.label: Each function is supported by multiple elements
athenaMake.comment: Use multiple methods to achieve important functions and to create redundancy and backup. Redundancy protects when one or more elements fail.
athenaMake.jeffReading: Jeff shaped the three roles to be distinct, not interchangeable. Their different instincts are the asset; collapsing them to one voice would make the system fragile.
athenaMake.source: Hemenway, T. Gaia's Garden, 2nd ed., p. 6.
athenaMake.techReading: Distinct role voices, multiple tests, multiple memory sources. Reduce-to-single is a lossy default. Three gates (product, code, arch) supporting the quality function via different lenses.

athenaMake.name: hemenway-get-a-yield
athenaMake.label: Get a yield
athenaMake.comment: Grow for both immediate and long-term rewards. A designer's discipline as much as a system property — listed under Hemenway's 'Principles Based on Attitudes.'
athenaMake.jeffReading: Jeff measures himself by what ships, not what he knows. The 'no dark work' principle is his.
athenaMake.source: Hemenway, T. Gaia's Garden, 2nd ed., p. 7.
athenaMake.techReading: Visible yield per card, per session. No dark work. The demo is the learning moment. Short-term: a shipped card. Long-term: a pattern the team can reuse.

athenaMake.name: hemenway-least-change-greatest-effect
athenaMake.label: Make the least change for the greatest effect
athenaMake.comment: Understand the system you are working with well enough to find its 'leverage points' and intervene there, where the least work accomplishes the most change.
athenaMake.jeffReading: Jeff looks for root-cause invariants rather than surface fixes. The preference for 'fix the shape that causes the bug, not the bug.' Calls out agent-shaped solutions that mass-mutate instead of adjusting the rule.
athenaMake.source: Hemenway, T. Gaia's Garden, 2nd ed., p. 6.
athenaMake.techReading: Fix the invariant once, not the symptom repeatedly. One-line inventory exclude beats 2075-file front-matter prepend. Gates over sweeps.

athenaMake.name: hemenway-mistakes-are-tools-for-learning
athenaMake.label: Mistakes are tools for learning
athenaMake.comment: Evaluate your trials. Making mistakes is a sign you're trying to do things better. There is usually little penalty for mistakes if you learn from them.
athenaMake.jeffReading: Jeff models this — he will say 'I was wrong about X' and redirect without defending the prior position. Invites pushback rather than fending it off.
athenaMake.source: Hemenway, T. Gaia's Garden, 2nd ed., p. 7.
athenaMake.techReading: Gates, hooks, ceremony ROI audits, three-role interaction as mutual correction. The seams between roles generate the corrections. Self-regulation: systems correct themselves from their own signal; unwanted feedback is still information.

athenaMake.name: hemenway-observe
athenaMake.label: Observe
athenaMake.comment: Use protracted and thoughtful observation rather than prolonged and thoughtless action. In the garden, this may mean noting where the sun and its shade fall during the day, where water collects, and in which direction the winds blow. Think over seasons, years.
athenaMake.jeffReading: Jeff reads the board, looks at the screenshare, listens to stories before committing to a move. Decision-making starts with watching. Resists 'give me the first step' when the shape isn't clear yet.
athenaMake.source: Hemenway, T. Gaia's Garden, 2nd ed., p. 6.
athenaMake.techReading: Gemba, dashboards, mutual attention. Watch a role work before directing it. Read the board before acting on it. Loom principles → architecture → code: pattern cards before implementation cards; composition before primitives.

athenaMake.name: hemenway-optimize-edge
athenaMake.label: Optimize edge
athenaMake.comment: The edge — the intersection of two environments — is where resources and interactions are highest. A productive edge is where the most diversity and productivity are found.
athenaMake.jeffReading: Jeff's best ideas come in the margins — the 'what if' during a demo, the story dropped between cards, the side comment that reshapes a roadmap.
athenaMake.source: Hemenway, T. Gaia's Garden, 2nd ed., p. 7.
athenaMake.techReading: Seams between roles generate patterns. Margin of the spec produces new cards. The Clearing IS an edge between roles. Demo seeds — Jeff's reactions to live work — are the highest-signal intake channel.

athenaMake.name: hemenway-small-scale-intensive-systems
athenaMake.label: Use small-scale, intensive systems
athenaMake.comment: Start at your doorstep with the smallest systems that will do the job and build on your successes. Grow by 'chunking' — that is, developing a small system or arrangement that works well — and then add it to another one.
athenaMake.jeffReading: Jeff cards a tiny fix rather than a big reorg when he can. Prefers a pattern learned over a pattern imposed.
athenaMake.source: Hemenway, T. Gaia's Garden, 2nd ed., p. 6.
athenaMake.techReading: Ship small, narrow blast radius, bounded services, deploy rings. Smallest card that teaches, not largest card that ships. Chunking: a practice that works becomes a skill; a skill that works becomes a primitive.

athenaMake.name: hemenway-turn-problems-into-solutions
athenaMake.label: Turn problems into solutions
athenaMake.comment: Constraints can inspire creative design; problems usually carry not just the seeds of their own solution, but the inspiration for simultaneously solving other problems. 'You are confronted by formidable problems? Celebrate, for you have just encountered opportunities!'
athenaMake.jeffReading: Jeff's 'bugs not character' stance — treats recurring failures as design opportunities, not discipline problems. When tone drops, fix the routing; when a skill is fragile, fix the shape.
athenaMake.source: Hemenway, T. Gaia's Garden, 2nd ed., p. 7.
athenaMake.techReading: Every recurring failure becomes a gate or invariant. Today's push-bloat crisis → repo bloat card + gitignore rule + future filter-repo plan. Friction becomes structure. Creatively use and respond to change: refactor, retire, rename rather than fight decay.
